summary: A 104 x 64 x 42 block less a 100 x 60 x 41 cavity open at the bottom (2 mm walls and roof), as in the test (the issue's 100 x 60 x 40 box shelled outward 2 mm). R5 on the outer top edge (y = 32, z = 42, length 104) together with R5 on the concave inner roof/wall edge below it (y = 30, z = 40, length 100) in one fillet was refused as too large (largest 4 mm), although the two built one after the other; #1720 made the fit check count the material the inner round adds. The outer round removes 25(1-pi/4) mm^2 along 104 mm, the inner one adds it along 100 mm: the cavity corner (30, 40) lies 3*sqrt(2) = 4.24 mm from the outer round's ball centre (27, 37), inside its radius, so the removed region stays in material and misses the added one. #1720's test also refused R5 on the outer edge alone; SolidCraft PR #2852 later let it build (it leaves the inner corner 0.76 mm inside the round and reaches it only past 2*sqrt(2)/(sqrt(2)-1) = 6.83 mm), and the test on main builds it. The R7 refusals (outer edge alone, and both edges) are not expressible in the runner. Tolerances are 0.1 % of the outer round's volume. Volumes are closed form.
